sector: Driver education and road safety training (accredited in car and classroom academy)
founded_place_size: Established 2009 in Burlington, Vermont. Small: two instructors, roughly sixty learners a term.
about: Milepost is an accredited driving academy in Vermont running in car lessons and a classroom course. Two instructors, about sixty learners a term, mostly sixteen to nineteen with a steady number of adult beginners. Our reputation is that we are calm and thorough, and every learner leaves certain about what they are looking at. Everything we make has to earn the trust of a nervous learner and the parent paying for the course.
audience: Learners sixteen to nineteen plus adult beginners, with the purchase decision usually made by a parent. People who want reassurance that the school is careful and legitimate.
price_positioning: Mid, accredited and dependable. Sixty dollars an hour. Not a budget app, not a premium driving experience brand.

palette.name: Signal Green
palette.usage: The scenario number, with its 3 px Caution Amber rule beneath (type system signature move), and the scenario title, as on milepost_guide_2019.pdf, always on Route White. Never a ground, a panel, step text or callout text.

palette.name: Route White
palette.usage: The only ground: every text card and text panel, as the page ground of milepost_guide_2019.pdf. All type sits on it, never directly on road footage.

palette.name: Slate Text
palette.role: mandatory where steps, the callout or captions sit on Route White
palette.usage: Step lines, the callout and captions on Route White, as on milepost_guide_2019.pdf, and the stop glyph, drawn like the single dark ink of milepost_glyph_sheet.jpg. Never a ground or panel.

palette.name: Caution Amber
palette.role: mandatory as the 3 px rule beneath every scenario number
palette.usage: Thin rules only: the 3 px rule directly beneath the scenario number, and at most a short rule above the callout, as on milepost_guide_2019.pdf. Never type, a ground, a panel or a fill.

palette.name: Sky Grey
palette.usage: A footer or accreditation line and hairline rules only, as the footer of milepost_guide_2019.pdf. Never a ground, a panel, step text or callout text.

typography: Milepost runs a four step scale. Step 01, display, is Baskerville Display PT Regular at 72 px on 80 px leading with tracking of minus 10 units for the scenario title, and the scenario number sets in the same face at three times that size, 216 px, in Signal Green with a 3 px Caution Amber rule directly beneath it. The vertical cutdown title runs 64 px on 72 px, and the school name is the only other Baskerville setting, in Bold. Step 02, subheading, is Inter Semibold at 56 px on 64 px with tracking of minus 5 units for callouts, because Baskerville is reserved for the school name and scenario titles. Step 03, body, is Inter Regular at 44 px on 58 px, tracking 0, to a maximum of 65 characters. Step 04, fine print, is Inter Regular at 32 px on 42 px with tracking of plus 20 units for captions and the accreditation line. Inter carries tabular lining figures at every size, the printed guide sets body at 11 pt on 16 pt, and a step is never set in italic or caps.
voice: Calm, instructive, reassuring. One idea at a time, numbered where it helps, no slang and no drama. Speaks plainly to a beginner and to the parent reading over their shoulder.
brand_assets_status: Everything a learner currently sees from us dates to 2019 and looks it. The printer holds the press file for the guide, but the source files for our simplified sign shapes are gone: they only survive as a photograph of a sheet our first designer printed and taped to the wall, so those glyphs have to be recovered from that. No brand typeface was ever locked, so the type system is open for you to set to our legibility standard.
values: Certainty over style. A learner and a parent must always be sure what they are looking at. Nothing stylised, nothing that reads as styling over substance, consistency that shows the school is careful.

type_system.signature_move: Every scenario carries its number set in Baskerville Display PT Regular at three times the scenario title size, 216 px against a 72 px title, in Signal Green, with a 3 px Caution Amber rule directly beneath it. On the vertical cutdown the number scales with the 64 px title and the rule holds at 3 px.
rules: Never set a step in italic or caps.
Baskerville Display PT sets the school name in Bold and scenario titles in Regular, and nothing else.
Every scenario number sets in Baskerville Display PT at three times the title size, in Signal Green, with a 3 px Caution Amber rule directly beneath.
Inter carries every step, callout and caption, with tabular lining figures throughout.

Nothing stylised. A learner and a parent must always be sure what they are looking at.

palette_rules.distribution: Route White is the only ground: the scenario number, title, steps and callout sit on a solid Route White card or panel, never directly on road footage, as milepost_guide_2019.pdf keeps its type off the photograph. On Route White, the scenario number and scenario title are Signal Green, and step lines, the callout and captions are Slate Text, as on milepost_guide_2019.pdf. Caution Amber is for thin rules only and Sky Grey for a footer or accreditation line and hairlines only; together they take no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area and are never a ground, a panel, step text or callout text.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity, once a card or panel is fully on screen. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow, glow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over the road footage: text sits on a solid Route White card or panel.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules or glyphs, so no red stop sign glyph, and no gradient, glow, outline, drop shadow or metallic effect on any type, panel, rule or glyph: nothing is stylised.
palette_rules.photography: Road footage and road stills keep their own filmed colour and are never tinted or graded toward the palette. The warm low-sun cast of milepost_road_still_01.jpg and milepost_road_still_02.jpg is not pushed toward Caution Amber, the cool fog of milepost_road_still_03.jpg and milepost_road_still_04.jpg is not pushed toward Sky Grey, and the painted road markings in every take keep the colours they were filmed in.
